messages:
alex.m: customer reports internal API endpoint resolving to a public EIP after the infra migration. internal app -> svc.internal.redwood.example.com resolves to 3.121.45.67 (public) instead of 10.92.5.12. high priority, production errors.

sam.k: ouch. any dig output from inside the customer's VPC or pod? can they run `dig +short svc.internal.redwood.example.com @10.0.0.2` (their resolver IP) and `dig +short svc.internal.redwood.example.com` (default)?

jordan.l: also ask for `getent hosts svc.internal.redwood.example.com` from a host, and `curl -v --resolve svc.internal.redwood.redwood.example.com:443:10.92.5.12 https://svc.internal.redwood.example.com/health` to confirm TLS pathing.

alex.m: customer ran dig from a pod in k8s, attached output: ```
# from pod resolver (10.0.2.3)
$ dig +short svc.internal.redwood.example.com @10.0.2.3
3.121.45.67

# from node / host using default resolver
$ dig +short svc.internal.redwood.example.com
3.121.45.67
```

nina.r: that looks like split-horizon worked incorrectly. public hosted zone with same name might be winning or the private hosted zone lost VPC association. did we recently touch Route53 or run terraform that touches `aws_route53_zone_association`?

priya.s: checked infra-bot diffs — there was a recent change in account `prod-shared` that removed a VPC association for `internal.redwood.example.com` during a cleanup (PR #4021). infra-bot: can you show the last applied plan for that zone?

infra-bot: last plan touching route53_hosted_zone_association for zone `internal.redwood.example.com` was applied 2026-02-18 by @ops-team (terraform-apply id: tf-apply-78a). It removed association to VPC `vpc-0a1b2c3d` (prod-east-1).

sam.k: that explains it — without the private zone association, DNS falls back to public hosted zone (or global record). Request: re-associate the private hosted zone to the customer's VPC.

alex.m: customer says they see cached answers for minutes after we re-associate. any ideas to accelerate?

jordan.l: TTL likely still active in their forwarder or local DNS cache. Ask them to: 1) flush local resolver cache (restart `dnsmasq`/`systemd-resolved`) 2) check any upstream forwarder (firewall / NAT / on-prem forwarder). Also provide `dig +trace` to show where resolution comes from.

priya.s: sample commands to send to customer: ```
# check resolver chain
dig +trace svc.internal.redwood.example.com

# flush on linux
sudo systemd-resolve --flush-caches || sudo systemctl restart systemd-resolved

# on mac
sudo killall -HUP mDNSResponder

# if using dnsmasq
sudo systemctl restart dnsmasq
```

nina.r: also check VPC resolver endpoints / Route53 Resolver rules. If they have a forwarding rule to a central resolver, that central resolver might have cached the public A. Request they clear cache or restart the forwarder.

alex.m: customer provided `dig +trace` — shows delegation to public route53 and no private zone in delegation chain. they also run a third-party firewall appliance (forwarder) that does long ttl caching.

sam.k: short term mitigation: update the private zone record to higher priority (create internal CNAME pointing to internal IP) is not ideal. Better: re-associate zone + ask firewall team to clear forwarder cache. We should also verify there isn't a duplicate public hosted zone with the same apex that still has the old EIP.

jordan.l: I ran a quick AWS check: public hosted zone `internal.redwood.example.com` exists in account `org-public` with an A -> 3.121.45.67 (legacy external ELB). Private hosted zone exists in `prod-shared` but association with prod VPC was removed by terraform apply. We need to re-run infra PR to restore association. PR prepared: restore-vpc-assoc-429.

priya.s: created PR and started apply with `terraform apply -target=aws_route53_zone_association.restore_assoc`. Apply succeeded at 1884004520.

alex.m: re-assoc done. customer still sees 3.121.45.67 from pod queries. last_message_ts: 1884004525. They restarted pod, still cached.

nina.r: this is expected until forwarders/clients flush. Ask them to run: `kubectl exec -n app -it pod -- nslookup svc.internal.redwood.example.com` and `kubectl exec -n app pod -- cat /etc/resolv.conf` to confirm resolver addresses.

customer (via alex.m): reports forwarder appliance has TTL 86400 for that name and doesn't support granular cache invalidation. ops disabled cache temporarily, now resolution returns 10.92.5.12.

sam.k: good. postmortem actions: 1) add terraform guardrail to prevent accidental removal of route53 zone associations for prod VPCs (policy/terraform). 2) add runbook step for early detection (monitor for mismatch between private zone A records and expected internal IPs). 3) notify customer success about mitigation performed.

alex.m: tagging @oncall-bot to create an incident ticket to track follow-ups and RCA. :white_check_mark:

oncall-bot: incident created INC-2026-1491, severity: P2, assigned: sam.k, target RCA in 72h.

priya.s: note for RCA: check terraform drift detection frequency, add CI check that prevents PRs removing zone associations without explicit approval from networking.

jordan.l: adding steps I ran to reproduce locally if you need them: ```
# repro (local mimic)
# create two hosted zones (public vs private) same name, associate private to a VPC, then remove assoc and query from that VPC
aws route53 create-hosted-zone --name internal.redwood.example.com --caller-reference $(date +%s) --hosted-zone-config 'PrivateZone=true,VPC={VPCRegion="us-east-1",VPCId="vpc-xxxxx"}'
# then remove association and observe that queries resolve to public zone.
```

alex.m: thanks team. I'll send customer summary and next steps. closing thread after RCA. :pray:
